_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Divi's Laboratories (consolidated, Rs crore). Divi's reports one segment (APIs, intermediates and nutraceuticals); the company discloses a generics : custom synthesis split (generics include nutraceuticals) and the nutraceutical revenue every quarter. The engine runs on a single revenue-growth path; the three-line build (generic APIs ex-nutraceuticals, custom synthesis, nutraceuticals) sits in businessLines and the authoring script checks it sums to model revenue. Other income = treasury yield x opening cash and investments net of borrowings + small recurring items; no forex gains are forecast. Valued on P/E, as most of the street does.
_revenueWhy: FY27 +19%: Q1 +27.8% (Rs3,080 cr) of which only ~10% was constant currency (standalone, CFO 1-Aug-2026): the rupee fell to record lows after the West Asia war began on 28-Feb-2026, and exports are ~90% of sales. Management repeats 'double-digit growth no matter what' (Kiran Divi, 1-Aug-2026). For Q2-Q4 we assume ~8% constant-currency growth plus ~8% translation (fading by Q4 as the base catches up) = ~16%. FY28 +16% and FY29 +14%: no further currency help; commercial supplies from the three dedicated custom-synthesis projects (~Rs2,000 cr capex, validation batches shipped in Q1FY27, commercial 'by 2027' subject to customers' regulatory approvals), iodine contrast-media long-term contracts, four new generic DMFs (brivaracetam, ticagrelor among them) and nutraceutical capacity. Street FY27E revenue: PL Rs12,563 cr, JM Rs12,713 cr, HSIE Rs12,882 cr (all 3-Aug-2026); FY28E Rs14,721-15,818 cr.

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs10,560 cr. Company: generics 45% (including nutraceuticals) and custom synthesis 55% (CFO, 23-May-2026); nutraceuticals Rs946 cr. So custom synthesis = 55% x 10,560 = Rs5,808 cr; generic APIs ex-nutraceuticals = 45% x 10,560 - 946 = Rs3,806 cr (PL's Q1FY27 note shows the same split).

businessLines._why: Generic APIs: Q1FY27 +6% YoY (PL, HSIE) with volumes 'stable' and price rises only passing through solvent costs; +8% in FY27 with currency and the first of the four new DMFs, then +6% (launches offset continuing price erosion and Chinese competition). Custom synthesis: Q1FY27 +45% YoY (validation batches of the three dedicated projects plus currency); FY26 +20.5%. +26.5% in FY27 (H2 slower than Q1, no commercial dedicated volumes assumed before Q4), +22.2% in FY28 and +18.4% in FY29 (base business ~8% plus ~Rs1,000 cr a year from the dedicated projects at ~1.2-1.5x asset turn on ~Rs2,000 cr of capex) as the dedicated projects, peptide fragments and contrast media ramp up. Nutraceuticals: Rs781 cr (FY25) -> Rs946 cr (FY26, +21%), Q1FY27 Rs298 cr (+19%); +18% / +12% / +10% as capacity additions slow growth to the category rate.

_marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income): 31.0% (FY23), 28.2% (FY24), 31.8% (FY25), 32.6% (FY26); Q1FY27 40.7% on a 68% gross margin. Management: the gross margin is not 'consistent throughout the year' at 68% and the FY27 EBITDA margin 'would be the similar as last year' (Nilima Divi, 1-Aug-2026); the Q1 gross margin was helped by a ~Rs500 cr inventory build (three-month raw-material stockpile at high solvent prices and validation-batch work in progress). Offsets: the weak rupee (exports ~90% of sales vs imports ~40% of a Rs4,000-5,000 cr raw-material bill) and a richer custom-synthesis mix. Check: at a normal ~61% gross margin, Q1FY27 employee and other costs would still have left ~34%. FY27 35.5% = Q1 40.7% and ~34% for Q2-Q4 (FY26 Q2-Q4: 33.3%). FY28 36.0% and FY29 36.5% as custom synthesis rises from 55% to ~64% of sales; not the 37-38% pre-Covid margins management says it 'dearly wishes' for. Street FY27E: PL 35.5%, HSIE 36.6%, JM 38.3%.
_capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs2,520 cr on Screener's cash flow (auditor: Rs2,635 cr incurred); FY25 Rs1,438 cr. CWIP Rs2,034 cr at Jun-26; the three dedicated projects (~Rs2,000 cr) are ~70% capitalised; Kakinada Rs1,500 cr plan with Rs600 cr capitalised and two more blocks under construction; more 3,000-litre SPPS peptide reactors being added; Kakinada Phase 2 (4 blocks) under evaluation. Management: FY27 capex 'constant' unless a new custom-synthesis project arrives (23-May-2026). PL assumes Rs2,000 cr a year for FY27-28.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs463 cr = 5.36% of average gross block (Rs8,640 cr, Screener); Q1FY27 Rs133 cr (Rs532 cr annualised) after Rs451 cr capitalised in the quarter. The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP held flat), so 5.4% gives ~Rs560 / 670 / 770 cr in FY27-29E as the CWIP is commissioned.
_treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and investments net of borrowings (Rs3,476 cr at Mar-26 on Screener: cash and bank Rs3,414 cr + investments Rs69 cr - leases Rs7 cr). Interest income was Rs295 cr in FY25 and Rs284 cr in FY26 (AR FY26 note 17), ~7.7% of the average of the five quarter-end cash balances (Rs3,694 cr); in Q1FY27 non-forex other income was ~Rs71 cr (Rs64 cr reported incl. a Rs7 cr forex loss), ~8.1% annualised on average cash. Deposits reprice lower after the 2025 rate cuts: 7.5% in FY27E (Rs261 cr), 7.0% after.
_otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income only: miscellaneous income Rs8 cr in FY26 (Rs4 cr in FY25) plus small fair-value gains (Rs4 cr). Net forex gains (Rs48 cr FY25, Rs210 cr FY26, -Rs7 cr Q1FY27) are left out: they follow the rupee, which we do not forecast. FY27E other income = Rs261 + 8 = ~Rs269 cr vs Rs296 cr ex-forex in FY26 and Rs287 cr ex-forex in the twelve months to Jun-26; the gap is the lower deposit yield and the cash spent on capex.
_interestWhy: Rs24 cr in FY26 and Rs6 cr in Q1FY27, almost all the notional unwinding of the Rs456 cr interest-free refundable advance from a custom-synthesis customer (carried at amortised cost, AR FY26 note 14(c)); no bank debt.
_taxWhy: Effective rate 24.9% (FY25), 24.2% (FY26: Rs820 cr on Rs3,388 cr), 23.6% in Q1FY27; the new regime rate is 25.2% less small deductions. 24.5%.
_payoutWhy: Divi's has paid Rs30 a share (1,500% on Rs2 face value, ~Rs797 cr) every year since FY22, a 27-51% payout depending on profit (30.6% in FY26). We assume the habit holds with small increases: 25% / 23% / 21% of EPS = ~Rs29-34 a share.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, export pharma with long customer contracts: below-market sensitivity. 0.85 gives a cost of equity of 11.6% (no debt, so WACC = cost of equity).
dcf._tgWhy: Top of the house 5-6% range: global small-molecule and peptide outsourcing grows faster than nominal GDP and India gains share (BCG via AR FY26: Indian CRDMO USD3-3.5 bn to USD22-25 bn by 2035).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from 14% (FY29E) to 9% by year 15: Divi's grew revenue ~11% a year in FY16-26 (Rs3,776 cr to Rs10,560 cr) through a Covid boom and bust.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 35%, below FY29E's 36%: generic price erosion and new competitors in peptides cap the margin near today's level.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from 11-16% of sales (FY27-29E) to 8% by year 15 (FY16-25 average ~12%): maintenance at about depreciation (~4.5% of sales) plus growth capex at Divi's ~1.6x net-block turn is ~8% of sales for ~6% long-run growth.
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital is ~44% of sales (inventory ~346 days of COGS, receivables ~100 days on Screener): every rupee of extra sales ties up ~44 paise, which weighs on free cash flow in both the forecast and the DCF.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The three dedicated projects reach commercial volumes from late FY27, GLP-1 peptide-fragment and contrast-media contracts scale, and the rupee stays weak; custom synthesis grows ~30% a year and the margin returns to the 38% pre-Covid level.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Customers' regulatory approvals slip a year, the Q1 inventory gain reverses, generic prices keep falling and the rupee recovers; growth slows to high single digits and the margin falls back towards 31%, the FY23-25 average.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How most of the street values Divi's: P/E on forward EPS (Motilal Oswal 55x 12M forward, BOBCAPS 56x Mar-28E, JPMorgan P/E, PL ~61x FY28E implied); JM Financial, HDFC Securities and Macquarie use EV/EBITDA (HDFC's 39x = 56.5x P/E). 59.0x = Divi's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 of 55.9x (forwardMedian; no trough years: FY24 EPS Rs60.3 stayed above half of FY22's Rs111.5) x 1.0545 pharma sector factor (median of the eight-peer set's trailing P/E vs five-year medians at the 30-Sep close, excluding Divi's; PLAYBOOK 7c) = 58.9x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Sensitivities only: the median on EPS before exceptional items (FY26 Labour Codes), the ex-Covid window from Apr-2022, Divi's own +23% re-rating and growth. Bull 65.5x (75th percentile 61.9x x 1.0545); bear 50.0x (25th percentile 47.4x x 1.0545).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check on the same basis: Divi's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 (EV at the weekly close / next full-year EBITDA, computed in tools/authoring/DIVISLAB.ctx.js) of 38.5x x 1.0545 = 40.6x, rounded to 40.5x Sep-28E EBITDA, plus Sep-28E net cash. Street: JM Financial 41x FY28E, HDFC Securities 39x Q1FY29E. Bull 46.5x / bear 34.5x (75th / 25th percentiles x 1.0545).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.6% cost of equity (no debt), terminal growth 6%, operating working capital ~44% of sales.
